questions.enonce_markdown:
4. What were the main achievements of President Ahmadou Ahidjo in domestic and foreign affairs? In what ways was his Presidency regarded as being dictatorial?

**(7/7/6 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** **Ahmadou Ahidjo** was the first President of Cameroon (1960-1982): President of the Republic of Cameroon from 1960, of the Federal Republic (1961-1972) and of the United Republic of Cameroon after 1972, until he resigned in November 1982 and handed power to Paul Biya. His rule is remembered for the unity and development of the country, but also for authoritarian methods.

**1. Domestic achievements (7 marks).**
- **National unity and integration.** He led the reunification of 1961 (the Federal Republic), and replaced the federation by a **unitary state** after the referendum of **20 May 1972**, which he presented as strengthening unity.
- **One political party.** The **Cameroon National Union (CNU)**, founded in 1966 by the union of the main parties, was meant to bring the regions together and give political stability.
- **Planned economic development.** He followed a policy of "planned liberalism" with **five-year development plans**, with development of agriculture (cocoa, coffee, cotton, bananas and later the "green revolution" policy of the 1970s), industries and the discovery and exploitation of **oil** from the late 1970s.
- **Infrastructure.** Roads, bridges, ports, hydroelectric dams (for example Edéa-Songloulou and the Lagdo project on the Benue), the **Transcamerounais railway** extended to Ngaoundéré (1974) and the **SONARA refinery** at Limbe.
- **Education and social services.** The University of Yaoundé (1962), new schools and hospitals, and the national airline, **Cameroon Airlines** (1971).
- **Peace and stability.** His government put down the UPC maquis by about 1970 and kept the country calm, which attracted investors.

**2. Foreign achievements (7 marks).**
- **Membership of international organisations:** Cameroon joined the **UN** in 1960 and was a founding member of the **OAU** (1963).
- **Association with Europe:** the **Yaoundé Conventions** with the EEC (1963 and 1969) gave Cameroon aid and trade advantages.
- **Regional cooperation:** he helped to create **UDEAC** (treaty of 1964), the **Lake Chad Basin Commission** (1964) and the **OCAM** (1965).
- **Good relations with France and the West**, with French technical and military cooperation, while keeping a policy of **non-alignment and good neighbourliness**.
- **Diplomatic opening:** the recognition of the People's Republic of China in 1971, and a moderate role in African affairs (support for decolonisation without extremism).

**3. Why his presidency was regarded as dictatorial (6 marks).**
- **One-party rule.** Opposition parties were banned or forced to merge into the CNU (1966); there was no free political competition.
- **Restriction of freedoms.** Press censorship, restrictions on trade unions and associations, and ordinances against subversion and the spreading of false news limited freedom of speech and assembly.
- **Repression of opponents.** Detention without trial in camps such as Tcholliré, and the trial and public execution of **Ernest Ouandié** (1971) and the conviction of Bishop **Albert Ndongmo**.
- **A state of emergency and a strong executive.** The President ruled by decree and used emergency powers; the abolition of the federation in 1972 was seen by many Anglophones as imposed from above.
- **Elections with one candidate.** He was re-elected as the sole candidate in 1965, 1970, 1975 and 1980, and a personality cult grew around him.
- **Control of the economy and administration** by the presidency and the CNU, with little local autonomy.

**Conclusion.** Ahidjo gave Cameroon unity, stability, development and a respected place in the world, but he did so through a one-party regime that limited freedoms and silenced opponents.
